analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, adding head lines 729-735 (patch hunk at old 726/new 726). The paragraph describes tooling tests for the PR threat-review scanner. It covers a 31-batch workload fixture, stage-admission failure attribution, no paid work on manual GitHub job reruns, bounded runtime configuration, human review for incomplete outcomes, manual dispatch limited to unpaid preflight, and a scanner deadline below the job timeout. These are documentation of CI/reviewer tooling, not provider runtime. They touch no code paths for the WebSocket contract (TB-002), provider key custody (A-002/A-003), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), the SSD prefix cache (T-041), the fan helper (TB-010), or consumer data (A-001). The text is descriptive and does not loosen any control or change any documented trust assumption. The statement that every incomplete outcome requires human review is fail-closed, consistent with the existing merge-gate docs. I reviewed the unchanged surrounding sections only for context. Their security-relevant statements, such as isolated state, no production cache roots or keys, and no real credentials in tests, are preserved. The one remaining question is whether the described workflow and test behaviors actually exist in scripts and workflows outside the supplied evidence. That is a documentation-accuracy concern, not a security regression, and it is not provable from this PR. No new attack surface or threat-model gap is identified.
